controls.statement: Stop and rollback criteria are documented before launch.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned release record can objectively show that explicit stop and rollback criteria existed before the recorded launch time.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The authenticated release record contains nonempty stop criteria and rollback criteria whose effective timestamp precedes the launch timestamp.

controls.statement: Rollback has been rehearsed.
controls.primary_reason: A current rollback rehearsal can be proven by an authenticated execution record tied to the release artifact, configuration, and rollback procedure.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: A bounded rollback rehearsal completed and produced an authenticated result bound to the assessed artifact, configuration, and rollback procedure versions.

controls.statement: Rollback is compatible with database and event changes.
controls.primary_reason: Versioned migration and event-contract inventories plus fixed backward-compatibility tests can decide rollback compatibility for the release scope.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release manifest enumerates every database migration and event-contract change introduced by the assessed release.
The previous application artifact passes the approved compatibility tests against every inventoried resulting database schema and event contract.

controls.statement: The previous artifact and configuration remain available.
controls.primary_reason: The prior deployment record identifies exact artifact and configuration versions whose current retrievability and integrity can be queried.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The previous successful deployment record identifies the exact artifact digest and configuration version.
Both identified versions remain retrievable and match their recorded immutable digests.

controls.statement: Traffic shifting and load-balancer behavior are tested.
controls.primary_reason: An approved finite traffic-routing scenario matrix and authenticated test results can prove that both traffic shifting and load-balancer behavior were tested.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every scenario in the versioned traffic-shifting and load-balancer test matrix has a current authenticated execution result bound to the assessed configuration.

controls.statement: Cache and CDN invalidation are planned.
controls.primary_reason: The planning claim can be decided from a release record that maps each affected cache or CDN surface to an explicit invalidation action and owner.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every affected cache and CDN surface in the release inventory has a versioned invalidation action, trigger, owner, and verification step.

controls.statement: DNS changes and TTL timing are planned.
controls.primary_reason: A finite DNS change set can be matched to a dated plan containing old and new values, TTL changes, propagation timing, and reversal steps.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each DNS change in the release inventory has documented old and new values, TTL timing, propagation timing, execution order, and reversal steps.

controls.statement: Certificate changes are planned and monitored.
controls.primary_reason: Certificate changes are finite resources, so plan coverage and active expiry, handshake, and issuance monitoring can be checked from records and environment state.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every certificate change in the release inventory has a versioned execution and rollback plan.
Every changed certificate endpoint has active authenticated monitoring for expiry, successful issuance or renewal, and TLS handshake state.

controls.statement: Every deployment action is auditable.
controls.primary_reason: A sealed deployment execution manifest and append-only audit stream can establish complete event coverage for the finite actions in one deployment.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The deployment orchestrator produces a complete execution manifest enumerating every automated and recorded manual action for the deployment identifier.
Every manifested action has an immutable audit event containing actor, action, target, result, and timestamp.

controls.statement: Verify the deployed artifact digest.
controls.primary_reason: The expected release digest and the digest of the artifact running in the target environment can be compared byte for byte.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The digest reported by every deployed instance equals the immutable artifact digest in the approved release manifest.

controls.statement: Verify the deployed configuration and feature-flag state.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned desired-state manifest can be compared exactly with authenticated runtime configuration and feature-flag queries for the deployed scope.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved release manifest identifies the expected configuration version and every expected feature-flag value for the target environment.
Authenticated runtime queries equal the manifested configuration version and feature-flag values on every deployed target.

controls.statement: Verify database schema and migration completion.
controls.primary_reason: Expected schema fingerprints and migration identifiers are finite release inputs that can be compared with authenticated database state and migration history.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release manifest enumerates expected schema fingerprints and migration identifiers for every target database.
Authenticated database queries match every expected schema fingerprint and show every expected migration completed successfully exactly once.

controls.statement: Test login, logout, recovery, and privileged authentication.
controls.primary_reason: Capability declarations and fixed expected outcomes allow bounded authentication tests to prove coverage of login, logout, recovery, and privileged authentication.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Each applicable login, logout, account-recovery, and privileged-authentication scenario in the versioned capability matrix has a current successful execution result.

controls.statement: Test authorization using multiple roles and tenants.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned authorization matrix supplies finite role, tenant, action, and expected allow-or-deny cases whose execution can be checked exactly.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The applicable authorization suite exercises at least two declared roles and two declared tenants across the versioned allow-and-deny matrix and every case passes.

controls.statement: Verify public, authenticated, administrative, API, worker, and scheduled-job paths.
controls.primary_reason: Declared route, service, worker, and job inventories can bound each applicable path class and link every item to a fixed verification result.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The assessed capability inventory enumerates all applicable public, authenticated, administrative, API, worker, and scheduled-job paths.
Every inventoried path has a current successful verification result against its versioned expected outcome.

controls.statement: Verify TLS, certificates, redirects, CORS, cache controls, and security headers.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned endpoint policy can define exact TLS, certificate, redirect, CORS, cache-control, and security-header expectations for bounded network probes.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved endpoint inventory defines expected TLS versions, certificate identities, redirects, CORS policy, cache controls, and security headers for each endpoint.
Authenticated bounded probes of every inventoried endpoint match every declared network and HTTP policy expectation.

controls.statement: Verify CDN and cache behavior.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned cache contract supplies exact hit, miss, expiry, purge, variation, and CDN expectations that finite request sequences can verify.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every applicable scenario in the approved CDN and cache behavior contract has a current successful bounded request-sequence result for the deployed release.

controls.statement: Verify alerts and synthetic monitoring.
controls.primary_reason: Complete declared monitor inventories and fixed trigger or probe tests can verify active alert routing and synthetic monitoring for the deployed targets.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every alert and synthetic monitor in the approved production-monitor inventory is enabled and targets the deployed production scope.
Each inventoried alert route and synthetic monitor has a current successful trigger or probe result.

controls.statement: Compare canary and control outcomes.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned experiment definition can identify canary, control, metrics, and windows, allowing exact computation and storage of their outcome comparison.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The rollout record defines the canary cohort, control cohort, observation window, and comparison metric formulas.
An authenticated comparison result exists for every declared metric using the recorded canary and control observations.

controls.statement: Verify analytics and business indicators.
controls.primary_reason: An approved indicator registry can define exact analytics queries, windows, expected values, and thresholds that authenticated production data can verify.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release plan enumerates every applicable analytics and business indicator with its query, time window, expected value or range, and comparison rule.
Authenticated observations for every declared indicator satisfy its versioned comparison rule for the post-deployment window.

controls.statement: Confirm customer support receives expected telemetry and documentation.
controls.primary_reason: A versioned support handoff manifest can enumerate expected telemetry and documents, and authenticated delivery or access records can prove receipt.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release handoff manifest enumerates every telemetry view and document expected by customer support with exact versions and recipients.
Every expected recipient has authenticated delivery or access evidence for every manifested telemetry view and document version.

controls.statement: Maintain heightened monitoring for the agreed observation period.
controls.primary_reason: A signed observation plan can define the heightened monitor set and exact time interval, while monitor and telemetry records prove continuous activation.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved observation plan defines the start, end, and exact additional or intensified monitors that constitute heightened monitoring for this release.
Authenticated monitor configuration and telemetry records show every planned heightened monitor active throughout the entire agreed interval.

controls.statement: Stop expansion when predefined thresholds are crossed.
controls.primary_reason: Because the thresholds are predefined, time-aligned metric and rollout records can decide whether every crossing prevented further expansion.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The approved rollout record defines each expansion-stop metric, threshold, comparison operator, evaluation window, and associated rollout scope.
For every recorded threshold crossing, authenticated rollout events show no later expansion and show a stop action at or before the allowed reaction deadline.

controls.statement: Record the final go, hold, rollback, or incident decision.
controls.primary_reason: The requirement is to record a decision, so an authenticated release record with one allowed final state, actor, time, and release binding decides it exactly.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: The release record contains exactly one final decision from go, hold, rollback, or incident with an accountable actor, timestamp, and assessed release identifier.

controls.statement: Schedule follow-up review for deferred observations and temporary controls.
controls.primary_reason: Deferred observations and temporary controls are finite release-record items that can each be linked to a dated follow-up review with an owner.

primary_deterministic_clauses.statement: Every deferred observation and temporary control in the final release record links to a scheduled follow-up review with date, owner, scope, and release identifier.
